footnotes: ¹ The Japanese Diet, at its 1924-25 Session, voted an appropriation of 150,000 yen for the Unemployment Census, and an Imperial Decree was issued on March 22, 1925. See Iwao F. Ayusawa, op. cit., p. 63. According to the census, the term "unemployment" meant manual or salaried workers who, having the will and willingness to work, were unable to get employment. Accordingly, the following class of people were excluded from the figures of unemployment: Infirm people, persons incapable of working through illness, persons not willing to work, persons working for themselves, workers involved in strikes and lockouts.
